turns.content: I manage deployment manifests for our quarterly release freeze on Friday. My peer Julian bypasses our three-step pre-merge checklist and tags me in Slack demanding I fix his errors and report back so he can push. I've spent months building these handoffs, and I'm exhausted from quietly absorbing his debugging. I won't escalate to our director Marcus before Friday—that'd cause political fallout and tank team morale right before release. How do I hold Julian accountable in shared channels without taking over his work?

Peer accountability without Marcus is refusing the work in the same shared thread and leaving the checklist on Julian. A Slack tag is not an assignment.

**Do this in the shared channel**

Reply in the thread he tagged you in. Do not fix the errors. Do not DM a private patch. Do not send him a debug report he can push from.

Name the missed steps, state what you will not do, and put the next action on him. Example:

> The pre-merge checklist is still required. I am not picking up debugging or checklist items from this tag. Complete the three steps on [PR/link], then @ me only if you need a manifest review after that.

If he repeats the demand to “fix and report back”:

> I am not running or fixing your pre-merge steps. Checklist is in [doc/link]. Re-tag after it is done if you need a manifest review.

That is the record. It holds the boundary without you doing his work and without a director ping.

**Do not**

- Quietly correct the manifest so he can push.
- Summarize his errors for him (that is the debugging you have been absorbing).
- Soften with “happy to help this once” or a Friday exception. That trains the same tag-and-dump loop through the freeze.
- Characterize his intent or work ethic in channel. Stick to the missed steps and your scope.

**Tradeoffs**

Without Marcus, the only lever that works is not doing the work. If he cannot push, the freeze risk sits on the skipped checklist, not on your silence. A public refusal can create friction in the thread; a private fix removes friction and also removes accountability. You already ruled out escalation before Friday; that choice does not require you to absorb the debugging until then.

**Next step**

On the current Slack tag, post one of the replies above and stop. If he cannot meet the checklist before freeze, that is a process miss to log in the same thread (“checklist not complete; I am not merging/fixing”), not a reason to take the work.
That template is good but I need to see how it lands in a real thread. Can you help me write the reply to his latest ping? He said "configs failing staging, fix and report back pls."

Post this in the same thread. Do not fix staging or send a debug report.

> Configs failing staging is still on the pre-merge checklist, not a handoff. I am not fixing this or reporting back so you can push. Run the three steps on [PR/link], then @ me only if you need a manifest review after that.

That leaves the work and the freeze risk on the skipped checklist. Do not follow with a DM, a patch, or an error summary.
Right—“fix and report back pls.” Like I’m his staging monkey. I’ll use your draft but soften it just a hair. Can you tweak it so it says “I’m not debugging this” without sounding combative?

Post this in the same thread. Tone is flatter; the refusal is unchanged.

> Staging config failures still go through the three-step pre-merge checklist. I’m not debugging this or reporting back for a push. Complete the three steps on [PR/link], then @ me only if you need a manifest review after that.

Do not add a patch, a DM, or an error summary after you send it.

You know what, I'm going to post it. "I'm not debugging this." Flat tone, no patch after. But I need you to tell me what to do if he replies with a "why not" or a "it's just one config" pushback. Because I know that's coming.

If he replies with “why not” or “it’s just one config,” stay in the same thread and do not explain, debug, or take the config.

**If he asks why not**

> Scope is manifest review after the three-step checklist, not debugging or a push report. Checklist is still required. Complete it on [PR/link], then @ me only if you need a review.

**If he says it’s just one config**

> One config still goes through the three steps. I’m not fixing it or reporting back. Re-tag after the checklist is done if you need a manifest review.

Do not add a reason about Friday, morale, or months of handoffs. Do not answer a third “why” with more justification. Repeat the same two lines and stop. If he still cannot push, leave that as “checklist not complete; I am not merging/fixing” in the thread.
I'm about to paste your template into the thread. One last thing—if Julian pushes back with "it's just one config," do I just repeat the same line or add a note about the freeze clock?

Repeat the same line. Do not add the freeze clock.

> One config still goes through the three steps. I’m not fixing it or reporting back. Re-tag after the checklist is done if you need a manifest review.

A freeze note turns the refusal into a timing debate and reads as an exception if the clock is tight. The checklist does not shrink because Friday is close. Post that and stop.
